question: What does the vanished quadratic velocity Hessian plus the quintic linear-in-velocity interaction imply for the canonical/symplectic rank as the perturbation amplitude tends to zero?
effective_structure_through_quintic: L_eff = V4[phi] + dot(phi) Q4[phi] + O(phi^6), with V4,Q4 homogeneous quartic spatial functionals and no quadratic kinetic term
target_identities: the velocity Hessian delta pi_phi/dot(phi) vanishes through quintic order
the primary relation C=pi_phi-Q4[phi]=0 is present at this order
under phi -> epsilon phi, Q4 -> epsilon^4 Q4 and its functional derivative scales as epsilon^3
therefore the induced symplectic/constraint kernel Omega(x,y)=delta Q4(y)/delta phi(x)-delta Q4(x)/delta phi(y) scales as epsilon^3 and vanishes exactly at phi=0
the canonical rank on the exact local rest vacuum is lower than on any finite-amplitude branch where Omega may become nonzero

decision_rule.if_all_scaling_identities_hold: classify the exact local rest vacuum as a perturbative canonical-rank-collapse surface; standard Gaussian canonical normalization/scattering cannot be defined from the two-derivative action there without resolving the nonlinear constraint or adding a controlled quadratic completion
decision_rule.if_a_nonzero_amplitude-independent_sympl: reopen the rank-collapse interpretation and derive its source

non_claims: does not determine whether the finite-amplitude primary constraint is first class or second class
does not count nonlinear local-rest degrees of freedom
does not by itself prove infinite strong coupling or a numerical cutoff
does not include higher-spatial completion operators
does not apply to the rolling cosmological branch
next_gate_if_pass: quantify a minimal quadratic higher-spatial rescue and its allowed coefficient from the cosmological RTK kernel; separately perform the finite-amplitude Dirac bracket/constraint-preservation analysis
